provenance.review_type: Separate independent AI source reviews; not human validation
provenance.scope: Source-aware review of sealed outputs. No original answer rewriting, paid rerun, reference-label scoring or private event chronology certification. Implementation-agent audit retained separately.

findings: Figure 2 places the TKA exclusion in BTB. Conditional on assumed 0–100 bounds and Table 4 counts, LET-minus-BTB is .860–3.186; reversal would require a BTB score of 137. The approximate two-point shift is valid, but MCID alone does not settle substantial-impact risk.
The TKA eligibility restriction is known. Whether IKDC was measured and discarded or never collected is unknown. D2 concern can be justified without claiming verified outcome-available exclusion.

D3 N/N/PY/NI → High is the official branch, not an implementation error or proof of likely dependence. Willingness concerns on-site examination, not necessarily questionnaire nonresponse. Table 3 nonsignificance does not establish exchangeability.
D4 PN/Some concerns is defensible under official §7.3 p53 active-comparator, independent-interviewer and delayed-assessment circumstances. Unblinded subjective measurement does not force High.

verification_reported: All 44 source bases within published precommit windows
findings: The available-case posttreatment comparison is legitimate, distinct from the primary mixed-model effect. Posttreatment is one month after baseline; Table 2 At 1 mo is later follow-up.
The conditional single BPI item rule and approximately .90 correlations support instrument choice. Five-week MRI/one-month descriptions concern the same nominal visit, not a demonstrated switch.
D3 official NI-branch High and the .7038 remaining gap under extreme bounds were verified, without proving likely MNAR.
Participant notification, self-completion and explicit strong benefit expectations support D4 PY beyond unblinding alone, without quantifying reporting bias.
D5 NI/PN/NI is defensible. Exhaustive eligible-analysis/hierarchy language must not become a universal PN barrier.
